title: What's the plan for the former Military Circle Mall site, and how settled is it?
summary: What the records show as of November 26, 2026 about the former Military Circle Mall at 880 N. Military Highway. WHRO reported (September 1, 2026) that the City owns much of the mall footprint; Council approved its transfer from the Economic Development Authority on July 15, 2025. Council has since appropriated up to $600,000 for operating costs (April 28, 2026) and approved a $200,000 advance to the Economic Development Authority for site readiness studies (August 25, 2026), which the City’s letter calls a prerequisite for applying to the Virginia Business Ready Sites Program for infrastructure development; the advance is repaid from a $337,750 state site characterization grant the Authority has been awarded. The agreement names the work: a site certification report, geotechnical, survey, Phase I and II environmental, cultural resource, species, wetland and traffic studies, and a preliminary engineering report on water, sewer and transportation infrastructure; the Authority is to work in good faith to have them completed, and this review found no copy of the reports yet. In October 2025 Council approved the City taking on the mall's leases and its 1968 operating agreement from the Authority. News reports say demolition was priced at nearly $3 million against a $10 million budget approved in 2023, set to start in October 2026 and run about 15 months, with the studies due around spring 2027. What isn't settled: as of September 2026 the City had no master plan for the site, Sentara owns part of it, and the Ross Dress for Less lease was still being negotiated (WAVY reported in June that Ross effectively holds a veto inside the ring road, and that the City was putting the demolition out to bid without its consent). The adopted FY 2027-2031 capital plan names no Military Circle project (the demolition money was reported as approved in 2023, before this plan), and the City Manager said the East Side library and recreation center would go to the former Poplar Hall Elementary site instead, to avoid the site’s delays. The City's demolition project sheet (updated November 4, 2026) names Reclaim Company, LLC as contractor, gives a $2,880,000 project budget, and schedules mobilization for November 1, 2026, about three to four months of remediation, demolition beginning in early 2027 and completion in winter 2028 (the City's undated project page still says demolition is anticipated to begin in fall 2026). The City's project page says the site readiness assessments (environmental and soil conditions, stormwater, sewer and electrical capacity) are under way at the same time and will inform a future master plan; it publishes no findings, and a final redevelopment plan has yet to be determined. City Council approves agreements for the land, and state law requires a public hearing before the City sells or leases it, with exceptions such as a lease to a public authority.

what_would_help.text: Watch for the site readiness reports (expected around spring 2027) and the master plan to follow: news reports quote City officials saying the studies will inform how the site is redeveloped.

A sale or lease of City land generally needs a public hearing first, the formal chance to speak on the terms; a lease to another public body or authority of the Commonwealth is exempt, and the Economic Development Authority is described as a political subdivision of the Commonwealth, so watch for a lease to it. A sale to the Authority would still need the hearing.
Watch City Council agendas for an agreement with Ross Dress for Less or Sentara, who hold parts of the site; WTKR reported the Deputy City Manager saying redevelopment could come in phases.

The site readiness work is a set of named reports (environmental, geotechnical, surveys, traffic, utilities). When they are delivered, they are the records to ask the Economic Development Authority or the City for; state law requires the grant recipient to sign a performance agreement with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority that includes reporting terms.

records_to_request: The Military Circle demolition contract and its notice of award, with the bid tabulation for the 13 bids received in July 2026 and the schedule of phases.

The Virginia Economic Development Partnership's award letter for the $337,750 site characterization grant, the engineering consultant's contract and scope of work, and the site readiness reports when delivered.
The operating agreement and the Ross Dress for Less lease covering the Military Circle ring road, with any amendments and any correspondence on consent to demolition since July 2025.
Monthly operating, security and utility costs for Military Circle Mall since the City took title in 2025.

The Economic Development Authority's performance agreement with the Virginia Economic Development Partnership Authority for the VBRSP Accelerated Site Characterization Grant FY'26, and each Site Report named in the cooperation agreement (Phase I and II ESA, geotechnical, traffic impact, PER) when delivered.

The 1968 Military Circle Easement and Operating Agreement and its eight recorded amendments (Deed Book 1104, page 628, through Instrument No. 020027164), whose assignment to the City Council approved on October 7, 2025.
pending: Whether work on site actually began: the City's project sheet (updated November 4, 2026) lists the project status as Construction and schedules mobilization for November 1, 2026 and demolition for early 2027, but no City notice that either happened was found as of November 26, 2026. The City's undated project page still says demolition is anticipated to begin in fall 2026.
The demolition contract itself and its award amount: the City's project sheet names the contractor and a $2,880,000 project budget, but no contract or notice of award was found.

The 2023 Council action approving $10 million for demolition is reported by WHRO and WAVY but not yet found in a City record; Siren's legislation index starts with July 2023 meetings, so the FY 2024 adopted budget and capital plan are the next place to look. (News reports from April 2023 describe a first phase that demolished outparcels; that is not the mall teardown.)

The site readiness reports themselves: as of November 26, 2026 no copy was found; the City's project page describes the assessments as under way and publishes no findings, the Economic Development Authority's site and VEDP's refused this environment's automated requests, and the state's annual VBRSP report on grant awards and expenditures, due November 1, 2026, wasn't found published yet.
Whether Ross Dress for Less exercised its lease renewal option: the City's August 2025 rent roll lists renewal options on the lease without saying whether one was exercised.
